t: See where your money went last month
d: Paste a month of bank transactions and get a clear spending breakdown by category, with your three biggest leaks pointed out.
when: At the start of each month

steps.b: In your banking app or website, look for an option to export or download transactions as a CSV or PDF. A screenshot of the list works too.
Delete or cover account numbers, sort codes, card numbers and your address before you share anything. Merchant names and amounts are all the AI needs.
Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, attach the file or paste the list, and use this prompt.
steps.p: Here are my bank transactions for [month]. Group every outgoing payment into categories such as Housing, Bills, Groceries, Eating out, Transport, Shopping, Subscriptions, Kids, Health and Other. Give me a table with each category, its total and its share of total spending. Then list my 10 largest single payments, flag any payments that look like repeat subscriptions, and point out the three areas where I could most easily spend less. Don't give investment or financial advice, just describe my spending.

steps.b: Skim the table and tell the AI about anything it put in the wrong place, for example a supermarket shop that was really a birthday present.
Copy the category totals into a simple sheet with one column per month so you can see trends over time.

example: October total: £2,184. Housing £950 (43%), Groceries £412 (19%), Eating out £186 (9%), Transport £143 (7%), Subscriptions £67 (3%)... Easy wins: 11 coffee shop visits (£42), two food delivery apps, a gym membership with no visits since August.
tips: Never paste full statements with account numbers, and remember the AI can misread amounts, so check the totals against your bank app.
Ask it to compare with last month's table if you paste both.

Sort transactions into spending categories
Add category totals as a new month column

Delete account and card numbers from anything you paste. Keep merchant names, dates and amounts.

steps.h: Ask the AI to spot the repeats
steps.b: Paste the transactions and any renewal emails into your AI assistant with this prompt.

Below are three months of my transactions and some renewal emails. Find every payment that looks recurring (monthly, yearly or weekly). Make a table with: service name, how often it charges, amount each time, cost per year, and the date it next renews if you can tell. Sort by yearly cost, highest first. Then ask me which ones I actually use, one question at a time.

[paste transactions and emails]

steps.b: Answer the AI's questions honestly. For anything you're dropping, ask it to write a short, polite cancellation message or tell you the usual place to cancel, such as the app store subscription settings.
For subscriptions you keep, add a reminder a week before each yearly renewal so you get a chance to decide again.

example: Found 9 recurring payments, £742 a year. Top: Streaming bundle £215, Cloud storage x2 (£24 + £60, you have two), Fitness app £96 (last opened in June), Magazine £48. Cancel the duplicate storage and fitness app: saves £156 a year.
tips: Subscriptions bought through your phone are usually cancelled in your Apple or Google account settings, not in the app itself.
Check for free trials that quietly became paid ones.

t: Make sense of a confusing bill or letter
d: A plain-English summary of any bill, bank letter or official money letter, what it's asking of you, the deadline and a suggested reply.
when: When a letter or bill doesn't make sense

steps.b: Take a clear photo of each page, or copy the text if it came by email.
Cover account numbers, reference numbers, your address and date of birth before sharing.
Attach the photos to your AI assistant and use this prompt.
steps.p: Explain this letter in plain English. Tell me: 1) who it's from and what it's about, 2) what they are asking me to do, 3) any deadline, 4) how much money is involved and why, 5) what happens if I do nothing, and 6) anything that looks unusual or worth questioning. For debt or legal letters, a free advice charity can help you respond.

tips: Remove order numbers and personal details you don't want to share, then add them back to the final message.

when: Whenever you remember something on the go

steps.h: Record as things come to you
steps.b: Use your phone's voice recorder, or talk straight into your AI assistant's app. Say everything, like 'need to call the vet, buy milk, Sam's party is on the 14th'.
Paste the transcript or speak directly to your AI assistant, followed by this prompt.
steps.p: Turn what I just said into three lists. TASKS: each with a short title, a due date if I mentioned one, and who it's for. CALENDAR: any events with date and time. SHOPPING: items grouped by type. Keep each line short enough for a reminders app. If something is unclear, list it under CHECK rather than guessing. Today is [day and date].

steps.b: Copy tasks into your phone's Reminders or to-do app, events into your calendar, and shopping items into your list app. Some assistants can add reminders directly if you've connected them.
Do it at the same moment each day, such as when you get in the car or after the school run.

example: TASKS: Call vet about Max's jab (by Fri). Return library books (Sat). CALENDAR: Sam's party, Sat 14 Dec, 2pm. SHOPPING: Dairy - milk, butter. Other - birthday card, wrapping paper. CHECK: 'that thing for Mum', what was it?
tips: Use your phone's built-in voice assistant to set single reminders instantly, and save this recipe for longer brain dumps.
Never record while driving unless it's fully hands-free.

Give me: 1) what I got done this week in 5 bullets, 2) open tasks, sorted into carry over, delegate or drop, 3) next week's calendar with any busy days or clashes flagged, 4) a suggested plan of no more than 3 priorities for next week, with the best time slots to do them, and 5) one thing to celebrate. steps.b: If your plan includes scheduled tasks in your AI assistant and it can read your calendar, schedule this for Fridays at 3pm. Otherwise add a recurring Friday calendar event and paste in your calendar and tasks yourself.
Add the three priorities to next week's calendar as time blocks so they actually happen.
At the end of each month, update the goals in the prompt.

example: Done: booked boiler service, finished tax return, two gym sessions. Carry over: sort Gran's birthday present. Drop: re-paint shed (not this month). Next week: Wednesday is packed, avoid adding anything. Priorities: buy present (Mon lunch), plan half-term (Tue evening), call bank (Thu 9am). Celebrate: tax return done!
tips: Keep priorities to three. More than that and none get done.

tips: Always ask about allergies in the invite and label food on the day.
